events.title: Stone tools at Deep Spinney
events.summary: Biddenham's earliest archaeology comes from the Palaeolithic site of Deep Spinney, among the first major Palaeolithic discoveries in England. The tools were probably carried there by glacial flow rather than left where people used them.

events.title: Mesolithic flints at Oakley
events.summary: Flint axes and arrowheads found within the present village boundaries are dated to around 7000–6000 BC, some of the earliest evidence of people at Oakley. Iron Age remains were later found when the almshouses were built.

events.title: A henge at Newnham
events.summary: A Neolithic henge stood on the site of today's Tesco supermarket on Riverfield Drive, built some time between 4000 and 2000 BC. There is little sign of any major prehistoric settlement around it.

events.title: Beaker burials at Kingsbrook
events.summary: Excavations in 1995 beside the Bunyan Centre uncovered a late Neolithic or early Bronze Age settlement and ritual site, with three skeletons and a complete Beaker pot.

events.title: Barrow cemetery at Roxton
events.summary: A Bronze Age barrow cemetery of five ring ditches was excavated in the 1970s ahead of gravel extraction near the Ouse, revealing two urned cremation burials. The site is now a lake.

events.title: Hoard of 60 bronze axes
events.summary: In the 1860s a hoard of 60 socketed axes was found on a farm near Wymington, possibly the stock of a bronze smith. Flint tools also point to Neolithic and Bronze Age settlement in the area.

events.title: Mowsbury hillfort
events.summary: Excavation has shown Mowsbury Hill to be a univallate hillfort, ringed by a single rampart, with pottery dating it to the early Iron Age. It was occupied only for a short time; in the Middle Ages the site became a moated manor.

events.title: An Iron Age house at Bromham
events.summary: Quarrying for sand, gravel and limestone between 1969 and 1975 uncovered an Iron Age house. The pit has since been restored as a lake and nature reserve.

events.title: Settlement at Colley Hill Farm
events.summary: Archaeologists working at Colley Hill Farm in 2011 found a Middle and Late Iron Age settlement, judged to be of local and regional significance.

events.title: Enclosures and trackways at Great Barford
events.summary: Excavations show Great Barford was settled long before the Middle Ages, with Iron Age enclosures and trackways marking out a farmed landscape, along with cremation cemeteries and burials.

events.title: A farm at Odell
events.summary: Just before the Roman invasion a farm stood at Odell: two round timber buildings inside a fenced enclosure, with two cremation pits. Its later prosperity may have been tied to the Roman presence at nearby Irchester.

events.title: Settlement by Hanger Wood
events.summary: Trial digs before Stagsden Golf Course was built found a late Iron Age and Romano-British settlement: a ditched enclosure, pits, a possible hearth, pottery and an animal burial. Much of the surrounding woodland was cleared in this period.

events.title: Roman enclosures at Wymington
events.summary: Cropmarks, ditches, roof tiles and pottery about 700 metres south of the village mark a complex of enclosures probably dating from the 1st to 5th century. Third-century pottery, coins, a quern and jewellery have been found to the north-west.

events.title: Roman farmstead by the Ouse
events.summary: A Roman farmstead near the river was excavated in the 1970s before gravel extraction created what is now Priory Country Park. Roman bricks from it survive in the wall beside the marina, alongside stones from Newnham Priory.

events.title: Roman farmstead at Radwell
events.summary: Gravel digging north of Radwell exposed a Roman field and ditch system and the remains of two timber buildings, probably a farmstead.

events.title: Roman farmstead at Grebe Lake
events.summary: The land between Harrold and Odell has been settled since at least the 3rd century, when a Roman farmstead stood where Grebe Lake is now.

events.title: Offa of Mercia buried in Bedford
events.summary: The Mercian king Offa was buried in Bedford in 796. Tradition places the grave in his new minster, now St Paul's Church, or on the nearby bank of the Great Ouse.

events.title: Henry I builds Bedford Castle
events.summary: Built after 1100 by Henry I and later extended in stone, the castle played a prominent part in the Anarchy and the First Barons' War.

events.title: Caldwell Priory founded
events.summary: A priory of Canons of the Holy Sepulchre on the south bank of the Great Ouse, in the south-west of the town. It lasted until 1536.

events.title: Newnham Priory founded
events.summary: Simon de Beauchamp, son of Payn, founded the priory at Newnham, east of the town, around 1166. Its first prior, William, was appointed that year.

events.title: Siege of Bedford Castle
events.summary: Henry III besieged the castle after a dispute with Falkes de Bréauté. The siege lasted eight weeks and involved as many as 2,700 soldiers; after the surrender the king ordered the castle slighted. Part of the motte survives in an archaeological park.

events.title: Bedford School founded
events.summary: Founded by royal charter in 1552, it is one of the oldest boys' schools in the United Kingdom and is run by the Harpur Trust.

events.title: John Bunyan imprisoned
events.summary: Arrested for preaching in November 1660, Bunyan spent twelve years in the County Gaol on the corner of High Street and Silver Street. There he wrote Grace Abounding and began The Pilgrim's Progress.

events.title: Bunyan's congregation buys a barn
events.summary: In 1672 the congregation led by Bunyan bought a barn here for worship. The present Bunyan Meeting church was built on the site in 1849, and the John Bunyan Museum opened beside it in 1998.

events.title: The Swan rebuilt for the Duke of Bedford
events.summary: The 5th Duke of Bedford had Henry Holland replace the old Swan Inn with a Neoclassical building, serving as both hotel and Whig political headquarters. Its staircase came from the demolished Houghton House at Ampthill.

events.title: The Town Bridge is rebuilt
events.summary: John Wing designed the present bridge, replacing a medieval one said to date from 1224 and built with stone from the castle. It was widened in 1938–40.

events.title: The Midland Railway reaches Bedford
events.summary: The first station opened in 1857 on the Leicester to Hitchin line; the extension to London St Pancras followed in 1868. The present station, about 100 m north of the original, opened in 1978.

events.title: The Corn Exchange opens
events.summary: Designed by John Ladds and William Powell in the Italianate style, the new Corn Exchange replaced a smaller one of 1850 and was opened by the 9th Duke of Bedford on 15 April 1874.

events.title: Bunyan statue unveiled
events.summary: Sir Joseph Edgar Boehm's bronze of John Bunyan was unveiled on 10 June 1874, a gift to the town from the 9th Duke of Bedford.

events.title: The Panacea Society is founded
events.summary: Mabel Barltrop founded the society at 12 Albany Road, following the prophetess Joanna Southcott. Members believed Bedford was the original site of the Garden of Eden; their story is now told in the Panacea Museum.

events.title: R101 lost on its maiden voyage
events.summary: Built at Cardington and at the time the world's largest flying craft, the airship R101 crashed in France on 5 October 1930 during its first overseas voyage, killing 48 people.

events.title: St Paul's goes on air
events.summary: With BBC departments evacuated to Bedford, St Paul's became home to the BBC's daily worship during the Second World War, and the 1941 National Day of Prayer service was broadcast from the church.

events.title: Glenn Miller broadcasts from Bedford
events.summary: The BBC Symphony Orchestra gave concerts here from 1941 to 1945, and Glenn Miller broadcast from the building with the American Band of the Supreme Headquarters Allied Expeditionary Force.

events.title: The Higgins opens on the castle site
events.summary: Bedford Gallery, the Cecil Higgins Art Gallery and Bedford Museum were joined into one building in the Castle Quarter, completed in June 2013.
